title: Many tables and self joins
summary: Chain joins across the schema, and join a table to itself.

steps.title: Following the keys
body: Big questions cross many tables. Draw the path first, then write one JOIN per hop:
JOIN appointments AS a ON a.id = pr.appointment_id
JOIN patients     AS p ON p.id = a.patient_id
JOIN wards        AS w ON w.id = p.ward_id;
The order of inner joins doesn't change the result; the database picks its own order to run them. It only matters with LEFT JOINs.

steps.prompt: Arrange the joins so each ON refers only to tables already joined.
lines: JOIN appointments AS a ON a.id = pr.appointment_id
JOIN patients AS p ON p.id = a.patient_id
JOIN wards AS w ON w.id = p.ward_id;

steps.title: Drugs by ward
prompt: For each **ward** name, return how many prescriptions were written for its in-patients (**prescriptions**). Only wards that have some.
Tables:
- `wards(id, name, floor)`
- `doctors(id, name, specialty, ward_id, mentor_id)`: `ward_id` is NULL for a doctor without a ward; `mentor_id` points at another doctor
- `patients(id, name, born, ward_id)`: `ward_id` is NULL for outpatients
- `appointments(id, patient_id, doctor_id, day, status)`: status is `done`, `cancelled` or `booked`
- `prescriptions(id, appointment_id, drug, dose_mg)`
- `invoices(appointment_id, amount)`: one per completed appointment
solution: SELECT w.name AS ward, COUNT(*) AS prescriptions
FROM prescriptions AS pr
JOIN appointments AS a ON a.id = pr.appointment_id
JOIN patients AS p ON p.id = a.patient_id
JOIN wards AS w ON w.id = p.ward_id
GROUP BY w.id, w.name;
setup: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

steps.title: Self joins
body: `doctors.mentor_id` points at **another row of `doctors`**. To show each doctor next to their mentor, join the table to itself under two aliases:
SELECT d.name AS doctor, m.name AS mentor
LEFT JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id = d.mentor_id;
`d` and `m` are two independent views of the same table. LEFT JOIN keeps the doctors with no mentor.
Self joins also compare rows of one table: *pairs of patients born in the same decade*, *appointments on the same day for the same patient*.

code: JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id = d.mentor_id

steps.explain: `<>` removes (Ada, Ada) but keeps both orders. `<` keeps exactly one of each pair.

steps.title: Ward-mates
prompt: Return pairs of patients who share a **ward**: **patient1**, **patient2** (the one with the smaller id first) and the **ward** name. Each pair once.
Tables:
- `wards(id, name, floor)`
- `doctors(id, name, specialty, ward_id, mentor_id)`: `ward_id` is NULL for a doctor without a ward; `mentor_id` points at another doctor
- `patients(id, name, born, ward_id)`: `ward_id` is NULL for outpatients
- `appointments(id, patient_id, doctor_id, day, status)`: status is `done`, `cancelled` or `booked`
- `prescriptions(id, appointment_id, drug, dose_mg)`
- `invoices(appointment_id, amount)`: one per completed appointment
solution: SELECT p1.name AS patient1, p2.name AS patient2, w.name AS ward
FROM patients AS p1
JOIN patients AS p2 ON p2.ward_id = p1.ward_id AND p1.id < p2.id
JOIN wards AS w ON w.id = p1.ward_id;

steps.title: Mentor in the same specialty?
prompt: Some mentoring crosses specialties. Return each doctor whose **mentor works in a different specialty**: **doctor**, **specialty**, **mentor**, **mentor_specialty**.
Tables:
- `wards(id, name, floor)`
- `doctors(id, name, specialty, ward_id, mentor_id)`: `ward_id` is NULL for a doctor without a ward; `mentor_id` points at another doctor
- `patients(id, name, born, ward_id)`: `ward_id` is NULL for outpatients
- `appointments(id, patient_id, doctor_id, day, status)`: status is `done`, `cancelled` or `booked`
- `prescriptions(id, appointment_id, drug, dose_mg)`
- `invoices(appointment_id, amount)`: one per completed appointment
solution: SELECT d.name AS doctor, d.specialty, m.name AS mentor, m.specialty AS mentor_specialty
FROM doctors AS d
JOIN doctors AS m ON m.id = d.mentor_id
WHERE d.specialty <> m.specialty;

steps.title: Patient summary
prompt: Build the patient summary: for **every** patient return **name**, **ward** (NULL for outpatients), the number of **done** appointments (**visits**), and the total invoiced (**billed**, `0` if none). Sort by **name**.
Tables:
- `wards(id, name, floor)`
- `doctors(id, name, specialty, ward_id, mentor_id)`: `ward_id` is NULL for a doctor without a ward; `mentor_id` points at another doctor
- `patients(id, name, born, ward_id)`: `ward_id` is NULL for outpatients
- `appointments(id, patient_id, doctor_id, day, status)`: status is `done`, `cancelled` or `booked`
- `prescriptions(id, appointment_id, drug, dose_mg)`
- `invoices(appointment_id, amount)`: one per completed appointment
solution: SELECT p.name, w.name AS ward, COUNT(a.id) AS visits, COALESCE(SUM(i.amount), 0) AS billed
FROM patients AS p
LEFT JOIN wards AS w ON w.id = p.ward_id
LEFT JOIN appointments AS a ON a.patient_id = p.id AND a.status = 'done'
LEFT JOIN invoices AS i ON i.appointment_id = a.id
GROUP BY p.id, p.name, w.name
ORDER BY p.name;
